gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Trio 3 Pro's 300-nit side screens reach full brightness only with a power adapter plugged into the Trio's own USB-C port, or lines up each extender's 'one cable' and 'driver-free' claims as the cables, video-capable ports and driver each needs before both added screens extend (show different content).
standout_why: I compared against three pages. Dealectric's /best-triple-laptop-screen-extender (cited by ChatGPT) gives cables and driver per product but never says whether the two added screens extend or mirror, and says nothing about brightness on laptop power. UPERFECT's '8 Best Triple Screen Laptop Extenders' (cited) gives a driver note only for its own BE14BF, gives brightness only as headline nits, and never covers extend vs mirror. The Mobile Pixels Trio page is cited too but I couldn't open it (HTTP 429), so I can't check what it says. ChatGPT's answers say only that base M1/M2 MacBooks 'often need DisplayLink'. None of them puts the connection claims in one comparable unit, and none says the Trio's 300 nits needs external power.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. The Trio 3 Pro is still the best under-$400 triple for a laptop with two DisplayPort-capable USB-C ports (Windows, or M1/M2/M3 Pro/Max and M4/M5 Macs per Macworld). The table should add two conditions: on a base M1/M2 MacBook Air (Apple: one external display), the second added screen needs Mobile Pixels' driver, and the rated 300 nits needs a wall adapter on the Trio. UPERFECT BE14BF's one-cable setup is driver-only per UPERFECT. The 'driver-free' FOPO S7/S1/S11 rows could not be normalised today (sources blocked), so their cable footnote must stay unsourced and not be inferred.

findings.label: Brightness condition

findings.label: Cables and driver for both screens to extend
